proposal: The Mandate recommends housing higher education data at the Department of Labor to make postsecondary and workforce-training outcomes more transparent, place them in the context of broader trends, adjust real wages for regional differences in earnings and cost of living, and build a methodology for risk-adjusting institutional and program outcomes so they reflect value added rather than admissions selectivity (pp. 338 to 339).
remaining: Move higher education data collection and reporting to the Department of Labor (p. 338)
Adjust real wages for regional differences in earnings and cost of living (pp. 338 to 339)
Develop a risk-adjustment methodology for institutional and program outcomes (p. 339)

sources.title: U.S. Department of Education Announces Six New Interagency Agreements
Accountability in Higher Education and Access Through Demand-Driven Workforce Pell: STATS and Earnings Accountability (final rule, 91 FR 40136)
Fact Sheet: Trump Administration Implements Accountability Provisions of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act

status_summary: No transfer of postsecondary data collection or the College Scorecard to the Department of Labor was found. The Department's 2025-11-18 announcement of a postsecondary partnership with Labor covers administration of most Higher Education Act grant programs and does not mention data functions. A different instrument, the final rule of 2026-07-01 (91 FR 40136) implementing the earnings provisions of Public Law 119-21, compares completers' median earnings with those of working adults with only a high school diploma, drawn from the institution's state or from national data; the Department's fact sheet does not describe a risk-adjustment or cost-of-living methodology.

timeline.event: The Department of Education announced a postsecondary education partnership with the Department of Labor in which Labor takes a greater role in administering most Higher Education Act postsecondary grant programs; the announcement does not describe a data transfer.

The Department published a final rule (91 FR 40136) implementing the Public Law 119-21 earnings provisions through an earnings premium test; it takes effect on 2027-07-01 except two instructions effective 2026-08-31.

title: House higher education data at Labor with regional wage and risk adjustment of outcomes
uncertainties: Searches run: two by the researcher (ed.gov and news terms on College Scorecard, Labor and postsecondary data, IPEDS, interagency agreement); the reviewer ran none for this record and re-read the announcement, the final rule page and the fact sheet. The final rule's section on the geographic scope of earnings data was truncated in both reads, so a regional adjustment inside the rule cannot be excluded; the fact sheet describes a state or national comparison group only. The earnings data come from a federal agency with earnings data per the rule, not from Labor. College Scorecard changes since 2025 were not found. Absence of evidence rests on a limited search. Moving NCES to Census is tracked in c11-02. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register API searches (Education Department and all agencies), the Education Department proposed-rule listing as fallback because the Unified Agenda listing was unreachable, one congress.gov and govinfo search with a BILLSTATUS read, the Education and Labor newsrooms (the Labor listing was stale) and one news search found no transfer of higher education data to the Department of Labor and no regional or value-added adjustment of outcomes. The College Transparency Act (S. 2511), reported by the Senate HELP Committee and placed on the calendar on 2026-08-04, would build a postsecondary data system at NCES within the Department of Education with no Labor role, and the IPEDS collection notice of 2026-10-09 is an Education Department notice that names no change of collector; neither qualifies. Education Department proposed rules from 2025 were not listed, and enacted laws other than P.L. 119-21 were not read for data provisions.
